chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali bin 'Uqba, from Ayub bin Hurr, from Abdul-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Arrogance is that one disdains people and stultifies the truth.

key_terms.يَغْمُصَ: To disdain, to look down upon, to slight
key_terms.يُسَفِّهَ: To stultify, to treat as foolish or insignificant

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance (kibr) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines arrogance not merely as self-elevation, but as a dual failure: socially, by belittling others (*ghamṣ*), and intellectually, by dismissing the truth (*safah*). This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition that views *kibr* as a root spiritual disease that corrupts both one's relationship with creation and one's reception of divine guidance.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	With this chain of narrators, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali bin ‘Uqba, from Ayub bin Hurr, from Abdul-A’la, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
Arrogance is that one disdains people and stultifies the truth.
